3. Reusable Cleaning Pipeline¶

In [9]:
import pandas as pd


class DataCleaner:
    """Reusable cleaning pipeline for the Superstore workbook."""

    def __init__(self, path):
        self.path = path
        self.orders = None
        self.people = None
        self.returns = None
        self.log = []

    def _note(self, message):
        self.log.append(message)
        print(message)

    def load(self):
        try:
            self.orders = pd.read_excel(self.path, sheet_name="Orders")
            self.people = pd.read_excel(self.path, sheet_name="People")
            self.returns = pd.read_excel(self.path, sheet_name="Returns")
        except FileNotFoundError:
            raise FileNotFoundError(f"File not found: {self.path}")
        except ValueError as e:
            raise ValueError(f"A required sheet is missing: {e}")
        self._note(f"Loaded: orders={self.orders.shape}, people={self.people.shape}, returns={self.returns.shape}")
        return self

    def fix_postal_codes(self):
        df = self.orders
        df["Postal Code"] = df["Postal Code"].astype("Int64").astype("string").str.zfill(5)
        mask = (df["City"] == "Burlington") & (df["State"] == "Vermont") & df["Postal Code"].isna()
        df.loc[mask, "Postal Code"] = "05401"
        self._note(f"Postal codes fixed, missing left: {df['Postal Code'].isna().sum()}")
        return self

    def remove_duplicates(self):
        before = len(self.orders) + len(self.returns)
        self.orders = self.orders.drop_duplicates()
        self.returns = self.returns.drop_duplicates()
        after = len(self.orders) + len(self.returns)
        self._note(f"Duplicates removed: {before - after}")
        return self

    def clean_text(self):
        df = self.orders
        for c in df.select_dtypes(include=["object", "string"]).columns:
            df[c] = df[c].astype("string").str.strip()
        self._note("Text columns stripped")
        return self

    @staticmethod
    def _iqr_flag(s):
        q1, q3 = s.quantile([0.25, 0.75])
        i = q3 - q1
        return (s < q1 - 1.5 * i) | (s > q3 + 1.5 * i)

    def flag_outliers(self, columns=("Sales", "Profit")):
        for c in columns:
            if c not in self.orders.columns:
                self._note(f"Skipped missing column: {c}")
                continue
            self.orders[f"{c}_Outlier"] = self._iqr_flag(self.orders[c])
            self._note(f"{c} outliers flagged: {self.orders[f'{c}_Outlier'].sum()}")
        return self

    def validate_dates(self):
        bad = (self.orders["Ship Date"] < self.orders["Order Date"]).sum()
        self._note(f"Rows shipped before ordered: {bad}")
        return self

    def run_pipeline(self):
        return (self.load()
                    .fix_postal_codes()
                    .remove_duplicates()
                    .clean_text()
                    .flag_outliers()
                    .validate_dates())

4. Feature Engineering¶

In [11]:
class FeatureEngineer:
    """Adds analytical columns to the cleaned orders table."""

    def __init__(self, orders, returns, people):
        self.df = orders.copy()
        self.returns = returns
        self.people = people

    def add_profit_margin(self):
        self.df["Profit Margin"] = (self.df["Profit"] / self.df["Sales"] * 100).round(2)
        return self

    def add_shipping_duration(self):
        self.df["Shipping Duration"] = (self.df["Ship Date"] - self.df["Order Date"]).dt.days
        return self

    def add_sales_category(self):
        self.df["Sales Performance Category"] = pd.qcut(
            self.df["Sales"], q=3, labels=["Low", "Medium", "High"]
        )
        return self

    def add_date_parts(self):
        self.df["Order Year"] = self.df["Order Date"].dt.year
        self.df["Order Month"] = self.df["Order Date"].dt.month
        return self

    def add_returned_flag(self):
        returned_ids = set(self.returns["Order ID"])
        self.df["Is Returned"] = self.df["Order ID"].isin(returned_ids)
        return self

    def add_manager(self):
        self.df = self.df.merge(self.people, on="Region", how="left").rename(columns={"Person": "Regional Manager"})
        return self

    def run(self):
        return (self.add_profit_margin().add_shipping_duration().add_sales_category()
                    .add_date_parts().add_returned_flag().add_manager().df)

5. EDA and Statistics¶

In [13]:
import os
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns


class EDAAnalyzer:
    """Statistics and charts for the featured Superstore data."""

    NUMERIC = ["Sales", "Quantity", "Discount", "Profit", "Profit Margin", "Shipping Duration"]

    def __init__(self, df, output_dir="output"):
        self.df = df
        self.output_dir = output_dir
        os.makedirs(os.path.join(output_dir, "charts"), exist_ok=True)
        sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

    def _save(self, fig, name):
        path = os.path.join(self.output_dir, "charts", name)
        try:
            fig.savefig(path, dpi=150, bbox_inches="tight")
        except OSError as e:
            print(f"Could not save {name}: {e}")
        plt.show()

    def summary_stats(self):
        return self.df[self.NUMERIC].describe().round(2)

    def correlation(self):
        corr = self.df[self.NUMERIC].corr().round(2)
        fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 6))
        sns.heatmap(corr, annot=True, cmap="coolwarm", center=0, ax=ax)
        ax.set_title("Correlation Heatmap")
        self._save(fig, "01_correlation_heatmap.png")
        return corr

    def distributions(self):
        fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(15, 4))
        for ax, col in zip(axes, ["Sales", "Profit", "Profit Margin"]):
            sns.histplot(self.df[col], bins=50, kde=True, ax=ax)
            ax.set_title(f"Distribution of {col}")
        self._save(fig, "02_distributions.png")

    def monthly_trend(self):
        monthly = self.df.set_index("Order Date")["Sales"].resample("ME").sum()
        fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(12, 4))
        monthly.plot(ax=ax, marker="o")
        ax.set_title("Monthly Sales Trend")
        ax.set_ylabel("Sales")
        self._save(fig, "03_monthly_sales_trend.png")
        return monthly

6. Advanced Visualizations¶

In [15]:
class AdvancedCharts(EDAAnalyzer):
    """Extends EDAAnalyzer with business-focused charts."""

    def category_performance(self):
        data = self.df.groupby("Category")[["Sales", "Profit"]].sum().reset_index()
        fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 5))
        sns.barplot(data=data.melt(id_vars="Category"), x="Category", y="value", hue="variable", ax=ax)
        ax.set_title("Sales and Profit by Category")
        ax.set_ylabel("Amount")
        self._save(fig, "04_category_performance.png")
        return data

    def region_profit(self):
        data = self.df.groupby("Region")["Profit"].sum().sort_values(ascending=False)
        fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 5))
        sns.barplot(x=data.index, y=data.values, hue=data.index, legend=False, ax=ax)
        ax.set_title("Total Profit by Region")
        ax.set_ylabel("Profit")
        self._save(fig, "05_region_profit.png")
        return data

    def discount_vs_profit(self):
        fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 6))
        sns.scatterplot(data=self.df, x="Discount", y="Profit", hue="Category", alpha=0.5, ax=ax)
        ax.set_title("Discount vs Profit")
        self._save(fig, "06_discount_vs_profit.png")

    def top_customers(self, n=10):
        data = self.df.groupby("Customer Name")["Sales"].sum().nlargest(n).sort_values()
        fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 5))
        data.plot(kind="barh", ax=ax)
        ax.set_title(f"Top {n} Customers by Sales")
        ax.set_xlabel("Sales")
        self._save(fig, "07_top_customers.png")
        return data

    def shipping_by_mode(self):
        fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 5))
        sns.boxplot(data=self.df, x="Ship Mode", y="Shipping Duration", ax=ax)
        ax.set_title("Shipping Duration by Ship Mode")
        ax.set_ylabel("Days")
        self._save(fig, "08_shipping_by_mode.png")

    def subcategory_profit(self):
        data = self.df.groupby("Sub-Category")["Profit"].sum().sort_values()
        fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(9, 7))
        colors = ["tomato" if v < 0 else "seagreen" for v in data.values]
        ax.barh(data.index, data.values, color=colors)
        ax.set_title("Profit by Sub-Category")
        ax.set_xlabel("Profit")
        self._save(fig, "09_subcategory_profit.png")
        return data

    def return_rate_by_category(self):
        data = (self.df.groupby("Category")["Is Returned"].mean() * 100).round(2)
        fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 5))
        sns.barplot(x=data.index, y=data.values, hue=data.index, legend=False, ax=ax)
        ax.set_title("Return Rate by Category (%)")
        ax.set_ylabel("Return rate (%)")
        self._save(fig, "10_return_rate_by_category.png")
        return data

7. KPIs and Automated Report¶

In [17]:
from datetime import datetime
from matplotlib.backends.backend_pdf import PdfPages


class ReportGenerator:
    """Builds KPIs, a text summary, and exports data and reports."""

    def __init__(self, df, output_dir="output"):
        self.df = df
        self.output_dir = output_dir
        os.makedirs(output_dir, exist_ok=True)

    def kpis(self):
        d = self.df
        orders = d.drop_duplicates("Order ID")
        return {
            "Total Sales": d["Sales"].sum(),
            "Total Profit": d["Profit"].sum(),
            "Overall Profit Margin (%)": d["Profit"].sum() / d["Sales"].sum() * 100,
            "Number of Orders": d["Order ID"].nunique(),
            "Number of Customers": d["Customer ID"].nunique(),
            "Average Order Value": d.groupby("Order ID")["Sales"].sum().mean(),
            "Average Shipping Duration (days)": d["Shipping Duration"].mean(),
            "Return Rate (% of orders)": orders["Is Returned"].mean() * 100,
            "Loss-making Rows (%)": (d["Profit"] < 0).mean() * 100,
        }

    def summary_text(self):
        d = self.df
        k = self.kpis()
        by_cat = d.groupby("Category")["Profit"].sum()
        by_reg = d.groupby("Region")["Profit"].sum()
        by_sub = d.groupby("Sub-Category")["Profit"].sum()
        lines = [
            "SUPERSTORE AUTOMATED ANALYTICAL REPORT",
            f"Generated: {datetime.now():%Y-%m-%d %H:%M}",
            f"Period: {d['Order Date'].min():%Y-%m-%d} to {d['Order Date'].max():%Y-%m-%d}",
            "",
            "KEY PERFORMANCE INDICATORS",
        ]
        for name, value in k.items():
            fmt = f"{value:,.0f}" if name.startswith("Number") else f"{value:,.2f}"
            lines.append(f"- {name}: {fmt}")
        lines += [
            "",
            "HIGHLIGHTS",
            f"- Most profitable category: {by_cat.idxmax()} ({by_cat.max():,.0f})",
            f"- Least profitable category: {by_cat.idxmin()} ({by_cat.min():,.0f})",
            f"- Best region: {by_reg.idxmax()} ({by_reg.max():,.0f})",
            f"- Weakest region: {by_reg.idxmin()} ({by_reg.min():,.0f})",
            f"- Worst sub-category: {by_sub.idxmin()} ({by_sub.min():,.0f})",
            f"- Correlation between Discount and Profit Margin: {d['Discount'].corr(d['Profit Margin']):.2f}",
        ]
        return "\n".join(lines)

    def export_clean_data(self):
        try:
            csv_path = os.path.join(self.output_dir, "superstore_clean.csv")
            xlsx_path = os.path.join(self.output_dir, "superstore_clean.xlsx")
            self.df.to_csv(csv_path, index=False)
            self.df.to_excel(xlsx_path, index=False)
            print("Saved:", csv_path, "and", xlsx_path)
        except PermissionError:
            print("Could not save data. Close the file if it is open in Excel and try again.")

    def export_text_report(self):
        try:
            path = os.path.join(self.output_dir, "analytical_report.txt")
            with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                f.write(self.summary_text())
            print("Saved:", path)
        except OSError as e:
            print(f"Could not save the report: {e}")

    def export_pdf_report(self):
        chart_dir = os.path.join(self.output_dir, "charts")
        pdf_path = os.path.join(self.output_dir, "visual_report.pdf")
        try:
            with PdfPages(pdf_path) as pdf:
                fig = plt.figure(figsize=(8.5, 11))
                fig.text(0.07, 0.95, self.summary_text(), va="top", family="monospace", fontsize=8)
                pdf.savefig(fig)
                plt.close(fig)
                for name in sorted(os.listdir(chart_dir)):
                    if name.endswith(".png"):
                        fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(11, 8.5))
                        ax.imshow(plt.imread(os.path.join(chart_dir, name)))
                        ax.axis("off")
                        pdf.savefig(fig)
                        plt.close(fig)
            print("Saved:", pdf_path)
        except (OSError, FileNotFoundError) as e:
            print(f"Could not build the PDF: {e}")

    def run_all(self):
        self.export_clean_data()
        self.export_text_report()
        self.export_pdf_report()

8. Memory Optimization¶

In [19]:
class MemoryOptimizer:
    """Reduces DataFrame memory by using smaller and categorical dtypes."""

    def __init__(self, df, category_threshold=0.5):
        self.df = df
        self.category_threshold = category_threshold

    @staticmethod
    def size_mb(df):
        return df.memory_usage(deep=True).sum() / 1024 ** 2

    def optimize(self):
        df = self.df.copy()
        for col in df.columns:
            dtype = df[col].dtype
            try:
                if pd.api.types.is_integer_dtype(dtype):
                    df[col] = pd.to_numeric(df[col], downcast="integer")
                elif pd.api.types.is_string_dtype(dtype) or dtype == "object":
                    if df[col].nunique() / len(df) < self.category_threshold:
                        df[col] = df[col].astype("category")
            except (ValueError, TypeError) as e:
                print(f"Skipped {col}: {e}")
        return df

    def report(self):
        optimized = self.optimize()
        before, after = self.size_mb(self.df), self.size_mb(optimized)
        print(f"Before: {before:.2f} MB")
        print(f"After:  {after:.2f} MB")
        print(f"Saved:  {(1 - after / before) * 100:.1f}%")
        return optimized

    charts.return_rate_by_category()

    ReportGenerator(df).run_all()

Conclusions¶

  • Sales and profit grew every year from 2016 to 2019.
  • Discount and Profit Margin have a strong negative correlation (-0.86).
  • Technology is the most profitable category; Furniture has high sales but low profit.
  • Tables, Bookcases, and Supplies lose money overall.
  • West is the best region; Central is the weakest.
